name: Clonazepam
meta: Psychotropic substance under the NDPS Act, 1985 and Schedule H/H1 of the Drugs &
sections: Off-white to light yellow crystalline powder, insoluble in water.
One of the Roche 1,4-benzodiazepines; widely used for seizure disorders and panic disorder. First approval/introduction: Patented 1960, marketed 1964; US FDA 1975 (Roche).

Enhances GABA-A receptor-mediated inhibitory neurotransmission; has potent anticonvulsant and anti-panic activity and some serotonergic effects. Receptor / target profile: Binds the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors, increasing the effect of GABA; also has serotonergic activity.
Hepatic – CYP3A4 nitro-reduction to 7-aminoclonazepam, then acetylation
Summary: Bioavailability ~90%; Tmax 1–4 h. ~85% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP3A4 (nitro-reduction). Half-life 30–40 h.
Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia
Seizure disorders – Lennox–Gastaut syndrome, akinetic and myoclonic seizures, absence seizures refractory to succinimides
Adjunct in acute mania, restless legs syndrome, REM sleep behaviour disorder (off-label)
Panic disorder: 0.25 mg twice daily, increase to 1 mg/day after 3 days; max 4 mg/day
Seizures (adults): 0.5 mg three times daily, increase by 0.5–1 mg every 3 days; max 20 mg/day
Taper by 0.125 mg twice daily every 3 days when stopping
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Seizures: 0.01–0.03 mg/kg/day initially; hypersalivation; behavioural effects.
Avoid; risk of neonatal sedation and withdrawal.
Dependence, abuse and withdrawal – use lowest effective dose for shortest time; taper
Alcohol, antihistamines, antipsychotics, other CNS depressants
Sedation, respiratory function, dependence; LFTs and CBC on long-term therapy.
Somnolence, confusion, ataxia, hypotonia, respiratory depression, coma. Supportive care; flumazenil with caution.
Rosenbaum et al., J Clin Psychopharmacol 1997 – clonazepam 1–2 mg/day effective in panic disorder.
Long-standing use in absence, myoclonic and Lennox–Gastaut seizures.
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
